We know who you are. You are Jesus and we're supposed to worship you, but we're going to have to kill you because you are a threat to the people. You're a threat to their happiness.

The grandchild will say to Jesus, "We create good in this world by being evil, and your presence will destroy this; therefore, we must destroy you."

This is from the brothers K maz. They do not love them at all but come to give their life for them. Instead of taking possession of man's freedom, they increase it and burden the spiritual kingdom of mankind with its suffering forever.

Okay. So what he's saying is that you came to this world to free people, telling them there's a spark inside them that they don't have to be slaves; they can go wherever they want. But this just confuses people, traps them in their own fear and anxiety, making life complicated. Keep on going.

Thou did desire man's free love, enticed by thee. In place of the rigid Asian law, men must decide for themselves what is good and evil with only thy image as their guide.

This is really annoying for people because before your teacher would tell them what is good and evil; now the teacher says you guys decide, creating complete chaos. People just want to be told what to do. For example, at 5:00 we're having dinner at Pizza Hut; people don't want to think about it.

They will cry aloud that the truth is not in thee because they could not have been left in greater confusion and suffering than thou has caused by laying upon them so many cares and unanswerable problems. You are creating all this anxiety in people for no particular reason, freeing them only good for the minority of people who can think for themselves.

What about everyone else? How are the other weak ones to blame because they cannot endure what the strong have endured? Can thou simply come to the elect for the elect? But if so, it is a mystery and we cannot understand it. If it is a mystery, we too have a right to preach a mystery and teach them that it's not the free judgment of their hearts but a mystery which they must follow blindly even against their conscience.

So we have John. Okay. What he's saying again is your freedom is only good for those who can think for themselves; what about everyone else? We created complete chaos so people will not be forced to obey us, corrupting your teachings.

We have corrected thy work and funded it upon miracle, mystery, and authority, leading them like sheep and lifting the terrible gift that brought such suffering from their hearts. Were we right teaching them this? Do we love mankind so meekly acknowledging their feelessness, lovingly enlightening their burden, and permitting their weak nature to sing or sanction?

Why has thou come now to ponder us?
